lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and planning: defining the actual problem before solving it

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic defining the actual problem before solving it task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character in charge of a shared resource is told 'the problem' is that people are careless or don't care, and works through a short set of clues to determine what is actually causing the pattern, before any solution is suggested.
safetyNotes: The scenario is fictional and does not require the learner to name or diagnose any real person or group they know.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What made the stated problem ('carelessness') easy to believe, even though it wasn't the whole picture? What question would have caught this sooner?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Evidence sorting accuracy: Clues are sorted correctly into supporting vs. not-supporting the stated problem, with reasoning given. | Root-problem statement quality: Statement names a distinct root problem that accounts for the clues. | Reflection on jumping to solutions: Reflection names a specific reason the stated problem seemed believable. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner list one additional clue that, if it turned up, would make them doubt their own root-problem statement, and explain what they would do to check it.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic defining the actual problem before solving it task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: defining the actual problem before solving it worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character in charge of a shared resource is told 'the problem' is that people are careless or don't care, and works through a short set of clues to determine what is actually causing the pattern, before any solution is suggested.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact defining the actual problem before solving it decision or action.
Model move 2: Before looking at the clues, write down what the stated problem is pushing you toward.
Model move 3: Read each clue in the provided evidence list and sort it as either supporting the stated problem (carelessness) or pointing to a different cause.

Model check: Evidence sorting accuracy: Clues are sorted correctly into supporting vs. not-supporting the stated problem, with reasoning given. | Root-problem statement quality: Statement names a distinct root problem that accounts for the clues. | Reflection on jumping to solutions: Reflection names a specific reason the stated problem seemed believable.

resources.title: defining the actual problem before solving it action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for defining the actual problem before solving it.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: defining the actual problem before solving it coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character in charge of a shared resource is told 'the problem' is that people are careless or don't care, and works through a short set of clues to determine what is actually causing the pattern, before any solution is suggested.
Coach direction: Before looking at the clues, write down what the stated problem is pushing you toward.
Learner prompt: Based only on the stated problem ('people keep losing tools'), what is the first fix you would reach for?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: defining the actual problem before solving it complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read each clue in the provided evidence list and sort it as either supporting the stated problem (carelessness) or pointing to a different cause.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I sorted each clue as either supporting carelessness or pointing to a different cause.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I can name at least one clue that does not fit the carelessness explanation.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: defining the actual problem before solving it minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What made the stated problem ('carelessness') easy to believe, even though it wasn't the whole picture? What question would have caught this sooner?

Success checks: Evidence sorting accuracy: Clues are sorted correctly into supporting vs. not-supporting the stated problem, with reasoning given. | Root-problem statement quality: Statement names a distinct root problem that accounts for the clues. | Reflection on jumping to solutions: Reflection names a specific reason the stated problem seemed believable.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: defining the actual problem before solving it supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional defining the actual problem before solving it condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Evidence sorting accuracy: Clues are sorted correctly into supporting vs. not-supporting the stated problem, with reasoning given. | Root-problem statement quality: Statement names a distinct root problem that accounts for the clues. | Reflection on jumping to solutions: Reflection names a specific reason the stated problem seemed believable..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner reads a provided fictional scenario in which a character in charge of a shared resource is told 'the problem' is that people are careless or don't care, and works through a short set of clues to determine what is actually causing the pattern, before any solution is suggested.
guidedFirstAttempt.prompt: Based only on the stated problem ('people keep losing tools'), what is the first fix you would reach for?
coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.
Give feedback against one observable success check.

simulationRoute.title: defining the actual problem before solving it — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the defining the actual problem before solving it task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: What made the stated problem ('carelessness') easy to believe, even though it wasn't the whole picture? What question would have caught this sooner?

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Evidence sorting accuracy: Clues are sorted correctly into supporting vs. not-supporting the stated problem, with reasoning given. | Root-problem statement quality: Statement names a distinct root problem that accounts for the clues. | Reflection on jumping to solutions: Reflection names a specific reason the stated problem seemed believable.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u05-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
